text:
Owen Michaels is an undrafted rookie from Detroit by way of Western Michigan, and 18 games into his NHL career he's one of the stories on Edmonton's depth chart. He has two goals and four points at about 12 and a half minutes a night. The New York Times asked late last month whether he needs time in the minors, which is the question every young depth forward on a contender faces.

The five-on-five numbers explain why. Edmonton has taken just 32% of the expected goals with him on the ice, more than 20 points worse than without him, the biggest gap on the team. Some of that is bad luck too: the Oilers have scored 4.7 fewer goals than the chances deserve in his minutes, and our numbers flag him as due.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has seven games of him, too few to show a clear strength or weakness. Our range has him at 6 to 15 goals over a full season, assuming he keeps the job. With Isaac Howard out, he probably will for a while. The test is whether his line can stop spending shifts in its own end.
headline: Michaels and the minors question
